title: Weak Epp over a perfect residue field
statement: Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Local means that the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal. Assume that $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ is perfect (characteristic zero, or characteristic $p>0$ with surjective Frobenius), and that $B/\mathfrak m_B$ is generated as a field by finitely many elements over $k$. There is a finite field extension $N/K$ such that, if $R_N$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $N$ and $C_N$ is the integral closure of $B$ in $(L\otimes_KN)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], then for every maximal ideal $q$ of $C_N$, the contraction $n=q\cap R_N$ is maximal, both $(R_N)_n$ and $(C_N)_q$ are discrete valuation rings [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $n(C_N)_q=q(C_N)_q$. Here finite means finite-dimensional over the base field, and the subscript red means quotient by the ideal of all nilpotent elements. No essential finite type hypothesis on $B/A$, completeness, separability of $N/K$, or stability under further extensions is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09F9, theorem-epp, perfect-residue finitely-generated-residue specialization used explicitly in Tag 09II (proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type), proof paragraph applying Epp to A' and B' at its finitely many maximal ideals.

proof.text: First handle residue characteristic zero. Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], its nonzero nonunit image in $B$ is $u\theta^e$ for a uniformizer $\theta$ and $e\geq1$. Put $S=A[t]/(t^e-\pi)$. The root-algebra theorem [lem-sbc-dvr-uniformizer-root-algebra] makes $S$ a DVR with uniformizer $t$. It is generated over $A$ by $1,t,\ldots,t^{e-1}$; put $N=\operatorname{Frac}(S)$. Since $S[1/\pi]=S[1/t]$ is a field (invert a nonzero element by its uniformizer-power expression), $N/K$ is finite. For any maximal ideal $q$ of $C_N$, [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], case (a), gives a maximal contraction $n$ and DVRs $(R_N)_n,(C_N)_q$. To identify $R_N=S$, note $S/A$ is integral by its monic equation. An $x\in N$ integral over $A$ is integral over $S$. If $x=u t^{-r}$ with $u$ a unit and $r>0$, multiplying a monic equation of degree $h$ by $t^{rh}$ gives $u^h\in(t)$, impossible. The uniformizer-power factorization therefore puts $x$ in $S$. Its base index is $e$, since $\pi=t^e$. Apply [lem-sfb-abhyankar-arbitrary-dvr-branches] with $d=e$ to obtain $n(C_N)_q=q(C_N)_q$. This finishes characteristic zero; below assume residue characteristic $p>0$.

source.place: Tag 09F9, first proof paragraph; Tags 09EV (root algebra) and 0BRM (Abhyankar)

proof.text: Write $l=B/\mathfrak m_B$. Apply [lem-sfb-finitely-generated-residue-perfect-core] to the given finitely generated field extension $l/k$. Every element of $l_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is separable algebraic over $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-epp-strict-complete-reduction] with a fixed uniformizer $\pi$ of $A$. This supplies the complete pair $A^{\prime}\to B^{\prime}$, its lower uniformizer $\pi^{\prime}$, and residue fields $k^{\prime}\subseteq l^{\prime}$ with $k^{\prime}$ algebraically closed and equal to the perfect core of $l^{\prime}$. It remains to construct a weak solution for this pair in the prescribed form required for descent.

source.place: Tag 09F9, positive-characteristic residue and completion reduction; ILO IV 3.2.3(ii),(iii) for the residue hypothesis

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-epp-compatible-coefficient-dvrs] to this complete pair. Obtain $A_0\to A^{\prime}$, $A_0\to D\to B^{\prime}$ with commuting square, residue fields $k^{\prime}$ and $l^{\prime}$, $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D=\mathfrak m_D$, and finite fraction-field extension $\operatorname{Frac}(B^{\prime})/\operatorname{Frac}(D)$. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-epp-finite-coefficient-triple] hold for $U=A_0,V=D,W=B^{\prime}$: completeness, algebraic closedness, the perfect-core equality, and finite upper fraction-field degree are precisely the preceding structural conclusions. It yields a finite weak solution $H/F_0$, where $F_0=\operatorname{Frac}(A_0)$. In equal characteristic $p$ take its prescribed separable-plus-uniformizer-root form.

source.place: Tag 09F9, last two coefficient-ring paragraphs; Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case

proof.text: In equal characteristic $p$, $A_0\to A^{\prime}$ is an isomorphism sending $t$ to $\pi^{\prime}$, by [lem-sfb-epp-compatible-coefficient-dvrs]. Transport the solution $H$ across this isomorphism. Its prescribed compositum form is then exactly the one required by [lem-sfb-epp-strict-complete-reduction]. The descent assertion supplies the required finite weak solution for $A\to B$. This handles equal characteristic; only characteristic zero of $K$ with residue characteristic $p$ remains.

source.place: Tag 09F9, k[[t]] paragraph and completion-descent paragraph

proof.text: In the mixed case put $K^{\prime}=\operatorname{Frac}(A^{\prime})$ and $M=\operatorname{Frac}(B^{\prime})$. Apply case (a) of [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure] to $A_0\to A^{\prime}$ and $H/F_0$. Choose a field factor $N$ of $(K^{\prime}\otimes_{F_0}H)_{\mathrm{red}}$; it is finite over $K^{\prime}$. Associativity identifies $(M\otimes_{K^{\prime}}N)_{\mathrm{red}}$ with a product of factors of $(M\otimes_{F_0}H)_{\mathrm{red}}$: tensor the finite product decomposition over $K^{\prime}$ and then reduce; images of nilpotents remain nilpotent after tensoring, and a finite sum of multiples of nilpotents is nilpotent. Thus quotienting the tensor product by their image ideal does not change its reduction. For a chosen local upper branch $T$, the weak solution $H$ gives a lower local DVR $S$ with $\mathfrak m_ST=\mathfrak m_T$. The normalization structure theorem applied to $A^{\prime}\to B^{\prime}$ and $N/K^{\prime}$ supplies an intermediate local DVR $R$. The maps $S\to R\to T$ exist by monic equations [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]: elements integral over $A_0$ in $H$ are integral over $A^{\prime}$ in $N$, and those integral over $A^{\prime}$ are integral over $B^{\prime}$ in the upper factor; localization at the contractions makes both maps local. Write a uniformizer of $S$ as $u r^a$ in $R$, and $r$ as $v t^b$ in $T$, using [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]. Locality gives $a,b\geq1$. The equality $\mathfrak m_ST=\mathfrak m_T$ forces $ab=1$, hence $b=1$ and $\mathfrak m_RT=\mathfrak m_T$. Thus $N$ is a weak solution for $A^{\prime}\to B^{\prime}$.

source.place: Tag 09F9, change from the coefficient DVR to the original complete lower DVR; Tag 09EM, normalized factors; index-one intermediate-ring argument written explicitly

proof.text: Apply the mixed-characteristic descent assertion of [lem-sfb-epp-strict-complete-reduction] to the finite weak solution $N/K^{\prime}$ just constructed. There is no inseparability restriction in characteristic zero. It produces a finite weak solution for the original $A\to B$. Unpacking its definition gives exactly the maximal contraction, both DVR localizations, and maximal-ideal equality required in the statement, for every maximal ideal of the upper integral closure.
